claims.text: The starting coating is a nanoscale multilayer of alternating FCC CoCrFeMnNi-type and BCC W-based refractory-HEA layers.
The starting multilayer has intact interfacial short-range order.
Sustained high load at elevated temperature disrupts interfacial SRO in the FCC/BCC HEA multilayer.
Local SRO breakdown produces a rejuvenated structural state.
The rejuvenated interface has increased free volume.
SRO breakdown enhances dislocation nucleation at the interfaces.
SRO breakdown facilitates interfacial dislocation motion.
Cooperative dislocation nucleation, climb, and limited glide accelerate creep in the multilayer.
Severe lattice distortion and compositional complexity promote progressive SRO breakdown under sustained loading.
A 2–5 at% Al or Ti addition can segregate to the multilayer interfaces.
Interfacial dopant segregation stabilizes SRO and delays its load-induced breakdown.
Preserving interfacial SRO reduces dislocation activity.
SRO-stabilized doped multilayers will have lower creep rates and delayed plastic-flow onset relative to pristine multilayers.
SRO-stabilized doped multilayers will accumulate fewer interfacial dislocations than pristine multilayers.
Pristine multilayers develop rejuvenated interfaces, higher interfacial dislocation density, and faster creep under the proposed conditions.
The proposed mechanism is sensitive to temperatures and stresses that activate dislocation climb and diffusion.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that failed dopant segregation or failure to influence SRO invalidates the intervention, whereas the falsification rule treats failure to obtain more stable SRO as falsification of the SRO-controlled creep mechanism. An unsuccessful intervention alone cannot distinguish intervention failure from mechanism failure.
